---
title: "Non-parametric augmentation"
description: "Augment observed panels with moving-block bootstrap or DTW barycenters."
---

`SynAugment.mbb` and `SynAugment.dba` transform observed series directly. They
do not fit a parametric generator and deliberately bypass the mean, standard
deviation, and lag-1 autocorrelation pinning used by `SynAugment.augment`.

Use only training observations as input. Augmenting from validation or test
values leaks future information into model training.

## Moving-block bootstrap

MBB separates a series into classical moving-average trend, seasonal, and
remainder components. It resamples overlapping remainder blocks and combines
them with the original trend and seasonal components.

```python
from synforecast import SynAugment

augmenter = SynAugment(seed=42)
mbb_df = augmenter.mbb(
    train_df,
    n_augment=2,
    seasonal_period=24,
    block_size=12,
    include_original=True,
)
```

When `seasonal_period=None`, SynForecast attempts to detect a period. When
`block_size=None`, it uses twice the detected period, or approximately the
square root of the series length without seasonality. The effective block size
is capped at `max(2, len(series) // 3)` so multiple blocks contribute even for
short inputs.

MBB is a good fit when local residual dependence matters and the observed trend
and seasonal shape should remain anchored. Each input series needs at least four
observations and one finite value. Missing values are interpolated before
decomposition.

## DTW barycenter averaging

DBA creates a synthetic series around each usable reference series. It finds
nearest neighbours with banded dynamic time warping (DTW), randomizes their
weights, and iteratively computes a weighted barycenter.

```python
dba_df = augmenter.dba(
    train_df,
    n_augment=2,
    n_neighbors=3,
    n_iterations=5,
    window_fraction=0.1,
    scale="reference",
    include_original=True,
)
```

With `scale="reference"`, series are z-normalized for alignment and each
barycenter is mapped back to its reference mean and standard deviation. Use
`scale="none"` only when the panel already shares a meaningful common scale.
The output length and timestamps follow the reference series, including when
its neighbours have different lengths.

DBA needs at least two usable series. DTW time and memory grow with series
length times band width, so reduce `window_fraction`, `n_neighbors`, or
`n_iterations` for long panels. Pairwise panel distances are computed once per
call in bounded parallel chunks in native Rust. Only the requested nearest
neighbors are retained, using O(number of series × `n_neighbors`) storage;
distance computation still examines every pair. Series without a finite observation are
skipped with a logged warning; `mbb` also skips series shorter than four
observations.

MBB computes its moving-average trend in linear time and reuses each source's
decomposition across all requested copies.

## Output contract

Both methods:

- return the same dataframe backend as the input unless `engine` is set;
- copy all non-target columns from the source/reference series unchanged;
- generate collision-safe string IDs such as `store_1_mbb_0` or
  `store_1_dba_0`;
- are deterministic for a fixed `SynAugment` seed; and
- run decomposition, block sampling, DTW, and barycenter updates in native Rust.

`include_original=False` returns only synthetic rows. Always compare augmented
training against an observed-only baseline over temporal holdouts; neither
method guarantees better forecast accuracy.

See [SynAugment: data augmentation](augmentation) for fit-and-simulate and
TSMixup workflows, and the [API reference](../../dataset.html) for every
parameter.
